title: Genetic characterization and development of novel microsatellite markers for Conogethes punctiferalis (Lepidoptera: Crambidae) populations in the Republic of Korea
content:
Abstract
Conogethes punctiferalis (Guenée, 1854) (Lepidoptera: Crambidae) is a polyphagous pest of agricultural and forest crops, but the genetic identity and fine-scale population structure of Korean populations remain poorly resolved. We combined mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) sequence analysis with the development and application of transcriptome-derived microsatellite markers to assess lineage identity and regional population structure. Korean sequences were analyzed together with reference sequences from China and Japan using phylogenetic reconstruction, COI-based molecular operational taxonomic unit delimitation, and haplotype-network analyses. We also screened 40 candidate microsatellite loci from a larval transcriptome, retained 10 polymorphic loci, and genotyped 326 individuals from 12 Korean populations and 1 Japanese population. Korean individuals were consistently associated with the East Asian COI lineage corresponding to C. punctiferalis sensu stricto in the present reference dataset. Across the full 13-population dataset, microsatellite analyses showed genetic differentiation in most pairwise population comparisons alongside extensive individual-level admixture, whereas divMigrate analysis of the 12 Korean populations indicated asymmetric relative connectivity among several population pairs. These loci provide transcriptome-derived nuclear markers for further evaluation of genetic diversity, fine-scale population structure, and temporal genetic change across geographic populations.
